summary: Sequence ID reuse in embedding ingest leading to cross-tenant candidate mixing and rerank tail-latency spikes
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported intermittent leakage of candidates from other tenant namespaces into their rerank responses. We observe embedding-IDs (sequence ids) being re-used across requests leading to candidate metadata collision in the reranker stage. Impact: incorrect top-k results returned to customer and large p95/p99 latency spikes in rerank pipeline while deduplicating conflicting IDs.

Impact:
- OmniSearch reported incorrect result sets (candidate IDs not matching their index) and user-facing search errors for ~2 hours.
- Elevated rerank p95 from ~120ms to ~2.8s during bursts.
- Potential cross-tenant data visibility risk (low volume confirmed).

Environment:
- prod-us-east, embedded ingress path through proxy v1.12.3 -> embed-ingest workers (autoscaled) -> reranker-v2 cluster.
- Affected models: text-embed-4k-v1 producing embed payloads with sequence_id header.

Timeline (local times):
- 2026-03-10 07:12 UTC: OmniSearch slack #support ping reporting anomalous candidates (attached screenshot).
- 2026-03-10 07:24 UTC: CI/Support triage, created this ticket.
- 2026-03-10 07:40 UTC: Initial logs show repeated sequence_id values across different tenant namespaces.
- 2026-03-10 08:05 UTC: Mitigation applied (ingress proxy flag to prepend tenant-namespace to sequence ids) — temporary reduction in leakage.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Send parallel embed requests from two tenants A and B through ingress proxy with concurrent batching enabled.
2) Force proxy to reuse connection pools (simulated with load tests).
3) Observe sequence_id header collisions in embed-ingest worker logs and duplicate candidate keys appearing in reranker input.

Expected behavior:
- sequence_id should be globally namespaced or unique per-tenant so no candidate cross-contamination occurs. Reranker should only see candidates from the requested tenant.

Actual behavior:
- Sequence_id reuse across tenant sessions allowed embed metadata collision. Reranker dedup logic attempted to reconcile IDs which added CPU work and inflated latency.

Attachments:
- OmniSearch screenshot (provided in support ticket), request traces, and extract of embed-ingest logs (links below).
steps_to_reproduce: See description steps: parallel embed requests from two tenants with connection reuse
Run load test with ingress proxy connection pooling to reproduce sequence_id reuse
comments: Priya Nambiar - 2026-03-10: Raised by customer via #support. Asked to capture example request IDs and time window.
Marco Perez - 2026-03-10: Running targeted grep on proxy logs to find reuse pattern; suspect connection pooling path in proxy version 1.12.3.
SRE-Triage (Liu Chen) - 2026-03-10: Reproduced locally with load harness. Observed seq_id recycled when TCP connection reused and per-connection counter persisted incorrectly.

Eng-Thomas (runtime) - 2026-03-11: Opened PR to add tenant-prefixing at proxy boundary and to bump sequence id generator to include monotonic tenant-scoped nonce. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-proxy/pull/483
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: proxy connection pooling keeps a per-connection counter that is not namespaced by tenant; when connections are reused across tenants sequence_id collisions occur.
Observed increased CPU and GC in reranker while dedup logic triggered; dedup implemented as a global in-memory set keyed by seq_id leading to cross-tenant lookups.
Search of recent deploys: ingest-proxy v1.12.3 rolled 2026-03-02 and changed connection reuse heuristics (related change: PR #460).
mitigation_and_workaround: Hotfix: enabled configuration on ingress proxy to prefix sequence_id with tenant-id (applied 2026-03-10 08:05 UTC) which cut leakage immediately for customers behind updated proxies.
Customer workaround: OmniSearch temporarily disabled aggressive connection pooling on their SDK (client-side) which reduced collision frequency.
Operational: Increased reranker dedup cache TTL to avoid expensive GC churn during spikes (temporary).
next_steps: (High) Ship ingest-proxy hotfix: ensure sequence_id is tenant-scoped + monotonic nonce (PR #483). Target deploy to prod-us-east 2026-03-12.
(Medium) Add unit/integration tests to simulate multi-tenant connection reuse and assert no seq_id collisions.
(Low) Audit other proxies/services that emit sequence_ids to ensure tenant namespacing is enforced.
Postmortem: Draft postmortem and notify security/compliance for cross-tenant exposure assessment.
related_security_notes: Potential low-volume cross-tenant exposure confirmed — data team to audit persisted indices for any leakage. Security notified 2026-03-10 09:15 UTC via #security-ops.
resolution: Workaround and hotfix deployed to ingress-proxy in prod-us-east. PR #483 merged and rolled to 30% canary on 2026-03-11; increased to 100% by 2026-03-12 02:10 UTC. OmnISearch confirmed return to correct results and p95 reduced to baseline. Postmortem scheduled; follow-up action items assigned to router and reranker teams.
